titel: De Groote Peel: a day trip from Hotel Asteria Venray
omschrijving: De Groote Peel National Park is a 43-minute drive from Hotel Asteria in Venray. Which trails are open, and how to end the day with sauna and dinner.
hero-sub: Raised bog, fens and boardwalks in a national park on the border of Limburg and Brabant, a 43-minute drive from your hotel room.
hero-alt: The Meerbaansblaak with birches and reeds in De Groote Peel National Park
oog-kop: De Groote Peel at a glance
t2-waarde: Buitencentrum De Pelen, Moostdijk 15, 6035 RB Ospel
t4-waarde: Visitor centre Wed-Sun, 10 am to 5 pm (Nov-Mar)
v1-kop: No forest, no heath, no polder
v1-p1: De Groote Peel National Park near Ospel is a 43-minute drive from Hotel Asteria. Peel means marshy place, and you see why straight away: between the birches and purple moor grass lie fens and pools, and across the wet stretches you walk on boardwalks, raised paths made of tree trunks.
v1-p2: This was once a vast raised bog that was almost impossible to cross. Most of the peat disappeared as turf, 'the gold of the Peel', into ovens and stoves. What remained has been a national park since 1993 and is internationally recognised as a wetland. When the water is low you can still spot peelpuisten: fossil tree stumps rising out of the peat.
v1-alt: Boardwalk of tree trunks across the peat of De Groote Peel
v2-p1: The quiet draws more than a hundred breeding bird species, such as the bluethroat, the stonechat and the yellowhammer. In spring and autumn migrating birds stop to rest, and with a bit of luck you will hear the trumpeting of cranes. Along the yellow family trail there is a bird hide and a lookout tower.
v2-p2: In autumn the mist hangs low over the bog and the landscape turns red, brown and gold. In winter it is above all quiet and wide open here, and you feel how big the raised bog really is.
v2-alt: Still pool with shrubs and reflected clouds in De Groote Peel
v3-p1: You start at the Buitencentrum De Pelen visitor centre in Ospel, opposite the park entrance. You park there for free, pick up a trail map at the desk and have a coffee or lunch at the Peelkiosk. From here the waymarked trails of 2, 3 and 6 kilometres set off. For a view over the area, drive to the Belfort Vossenberg near Meijel: a 22-metre tower next to six Second World War bunkers, with a walking trail that is open all year.
v3-alt: Buitencentrum De Pelen in Ospel, the starting point of the walking trails
tip: Come in the morning, park at the visitor centre and walk the blue trail of 6 kilometres: it stays open even when parts of the park are closed for the birds. Then have lunch at the Peelkiosk. Wear waterproof shoes, as the paths can be wet, and in winter do not go on a Monday: the visitor centre and the Peelkiosk are both closed then.
g1-tekst: From November to March inclusive, Wednesday to Sunday 10 am to 5 pm, with the Peelkiosk also open on Tuesdays in winter. From April to October inclusive, every day.
g1-alt: Information board of De Groote Peel National Park at the visitor centre
g2-tekst: From 15 March to 15 July inclusive and from 15 October to 30 November inclusive, parts are closed. The 2, 3 and 6 km trails stay open.
g2-alt: Sign about the birds of the Mussenbaan beside a fen in De Groote Peel
g3-tekst: Large car park at Buitencentrum De Pelen, Moostdijk 15 in Ospel.
g3-alt: Sandy path with signposts between the birches in De Groote Peel
g4-tekst: Welcome, but on a lead. Bring a poo bag: there are no bins in the park.
g4-alt: Heath with pines in De Groote Peel
dag-sub: Breakfast at the hotel, a walk in De Groote Peel during the day and back in the late afternoon for the sauna and dinner.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 7 to 10 am on weekdays and from 8 to 10.30 am at weekends. The visitor centre opens at 10 am and is a 43-minute drive away, so after breakfast you will be there in good time for a morning walk.
m1-alt: Breakfast buffet in the restaurant of Hotel Asteria
m2-tekst: Walk the blue trail of 6 kilometres over boardwalks and past fens, and have lunch at the Peelkiosk by the visitor centre. Plan your walk in good time: the park is open from sunrise to sunset.
m2-alt: Birch above a sandy path under a blue sky in De Groote Peel
m3-tekst: Back in Venray, warm up in the sauna. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 4 pm to 10 pm and Friday to Sunday from 12 noon to 10 pm. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m3-alt: Foot bath in the wellness area on the Top Floor
m4-tekst: End the day at a table in the hotel brasserie. The kitchen is open until 9.30 pm, and afterwards your room is just a lift ride away.
m4-alt: Bar in the brasserie of Hotel Asteria
kamers-sub: After a day outdoors, the sauna and dinner, there is no need to drive home. Choose your room; you will see the price for your dates straight away when you book.
kaart-regel: De Groote Peel lies near Ospel, south-west of Venray on the border with Brabant. The map also shows three other outings you can combine on the way or nearby.
kaart-naam: Buitencentrum De Pelen, Moostdijk 15, 6035 RB Ospel
kaart-alt: Map of North Limburg with Hotel Asteria in Venray, De Groote Peel near Ospel and three other outings
f1-v: How far is De Groote Peel from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: To Buitencentrum De Pelen in Ospel, the starting point of the walking trails, it is 49 kilometres, about 43 minutes by car. Parking at the visitor centre is free, just as it is at Hotel Asteria.
f2-v: Which trails are open during the breeding season and bird migration?
f2-a: From 15 March to 15 July inclusive and from 15 October to 30 November inclusive, parts of the park are closed to give the birds some peace. The waymarked trails of 2 km (yellow), 3 km (red) and 6 km (blue) stay open, as does the 7 km trail through the Paardenbegrazing (horse grazing area); you can pick up its map at the visitor centre. The trail from the Belfort Vossenberg is open all year. Check the signs at the entrance when you arrive.
f3-v: When is the visitor centre open?
f3-a: From April to October inclusive, every day from 10 am to 5 pm. From November to March inclusive, the desk and the shop are open Wednesday to Sunday from 10 am to 5 pm; the Peelkiosk is also open on Tuesdays in the winter months. During the Dutch spring half-term (voorjaarsvakantie) the visitor centre is open every day. The park itself is open from sunrise to sunset.
f4-v: Can I walk there with a wheelchair or pushchair?
f4-a: Yes. The yellow family trail of 2 kilometres starts at the visitor centre. It is paved and suitable for wheelchairs, mobility scooters and pushchairs, and the bird hide and lookout tower along this trail are wheelchair accessible. You can borrow a wheelchair at the visitor centre. The other trails are fairly manageable in dry weather, but you will need help at the boardwalks.
f5-v: Can I bring my dog, and can I cycle in the park?
f5-a: Dogs are welcome, but only on a lead. Cycling is not allowed in the nature reserve, except on the Mussenbaan cycle path on the east side (junction 94 to 5) and on the south side (junction 7 to 8).
f6-v: Can I still use the wellness area and have dinner at the hotel after my walk?
f6-a: Yes. You are back in Venray in three quarters of an hour. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 4 pm to 10 pm and Friday to Sunday from 12 noon to 10 pm. Tuesday is swimwear day. You can have dinner in the brasserie until 9.30 pm.

mariapeel.desc: Not walked enough yet? The Mariapeel near Evertsoord belongs to the same national park and is 29 minutes from the hotel. It is rugged, open and marshy raised bog, with the scars of peat cutting and traces of the Second World War, such as the crash site of a British fighter plane. Waymarked trails start from the car park at the Biologisch Station. In winter and during the breeding season, parts are closed.
mariapeel.credit: Photos: Jan van der Straaten (Saxifraga, CC BY-SA 3.0) and Aat van den Heuvel (CC BY 3.0) via Wikimedia Commons, cropped.

maasduinen.desc: Prefer woodland and drift sand to bog? De Maasduinen is a quarter of an hour from the hotel, between the Maas and the German border: over 4,500 hectares of woodland, heath, drift sand and fens. You choose your walking or cycling route at the visitor centre in Well.
maasduinen.credit: Photos: Lieblingsgouda, Steven Lek, Carelbullens and Jonathation via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA), cropped.

venray.desc: The centre of Venray is about 4 kilometres from the hotel. On the Grote Markt stands the Sint-Petrus' Bandenkerk, also known as the cathedral of the Peel, with a tower of almost 80 metres. Around the square you can have a coffee or lunch on a terrace.
venray.credit: Photos: Dosseman, giggel, WoodenSpoon and Sindala via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA and CC BY), cropped.
